items.title: Cultivating Attention on the Marks — and the Four Things It Accomplishes

items.zh: 復次，云何修習所緣諸相作意？謂即於彼彼諸相作意思惟。以思惟故、能作四事。謂即修習如是作意；又能遠彼所治煩惱；又能練此作意及餘、令後所生轉更明盛；又即修習此作意時，厭壞所緣，捨諸煩惱，任持斷滅，令諸煩惱遠離相續。是故修習如是所緣諸相作意。
items.en: Furthermore, what is cultivating attention on the object's various marks? It is attending to and contemplating each of those marks. Because of this contemplation, four things are accomplished: one cultivates such attention itself; one distances the affliction to be countered; one refines this attention and its companions, so that what arises later grows ever brighter and stronger; and, while cultivating this attention, one wearies of and breaks down the object, casts off the afflictions, holds firm to their severance, and makes the afflictions withdraw from the continuum. Therefore one should cultivate such attention on the object's various marks.

items.title: The Four Powers That Open Absorption, and the Four Kinds of Contemplative

items.zh: 復次，由四因緣，入初靜慮乃至有頂。謂因力、方便力、說力、教授力。云何因力？謂曾隣近入靜慮等。云何方便力？謂雖不隣近入靜慮等，然由數習無間修力、能入諸定。
items.en: Furthermore, by four conditions one enters the first dhyāna and so on up to the peak of existence: the power of the cause, the power of method, the power of teaching, and the power of instruction. What is the power of the cause? Having, in the past, drawn near to entering the dhyānas and the rest. What is the power of method? Though one has not [before] drawn near to entering the dhyānas, yet by the force of repeated, unbroken cultivation one is able to enter the concentrations.

items.zh: 云何說力？謂於靜慮等增上緣法，多聞任持，乃至廣說。即依此法，獨處空閑，離諸放逸，勇猛精進，自策勵住，法隨法行，由此能入靜慮等定。云何教授力？謂於親教軌範師所，或於隨一餘尊長所，獲得隨順初靜慮等無倒教授；從此審諦作意思惟，能入靜慮及諸餘定。如是顯示四觀行者。謂具因力者、方便力者、若利根者、及鈍根者。
items.en: What is the power of teaching? Having widely heard and retained the teachings that are the dominant condition for the dhyānas and the rest, and so on at length; then, relying on that teaching, dwelling alone in a quiet place, free of heedlessness, valiantly diligent, spurring and rousing oneself, abiding in the practice of the Dharma in accord with the Dharma — by this one is able to enter the dhyānas. What is the power of instruction? Receiving, from one's preceptor or master, or from some other elder, undistorted instruction in accord with the first dhyāna and the rest; then, closely attending to and contemplating it, one is able to enter the dhyānas and the other concentrations. Thus are displayed four contemplatives: one endowed with the power of the cause, one with the power of method, one of sharp faculties, and one of dull faculties.

items.title: Two Flawed Attainers: The One Who Relishes Dhyāna, and the One Who Reads It as a Permanent Self

items.zh: 復次，有四得靜慮者。一、愛上靜慮者，二、見上靜慮者，三、慢上靜慮者，四、疑上靜慮者。云何愛上靜慮者？謂如有一，先聞靜慮諸定功德，而不聞彼出離方便。於彼一向見勝功德，勇猛精勤；由此因緣，入初靜慮或所餘定。如是入已，後生愛味。
items.en: Furthermore, there are four attainers of dhyāna: one who relishes the superior dhyāna, one with views in the superior dhyāna, one with conceit in the superior dhyāna, and one with doubt in the superior dhyāna. What is the one who relishes dhyāna? Someone who has heard of the merits of the dhyānas and concentrations but has not heard of the means of release from them; seeing in them only surpassing merit, he is valiantly diligent, and by this enters the first dhyāna or another concentration. Having entered thus, he afterwards gives rise to a relish for it.

items.zh: 云何見上靜慮者？謂如有一，從自師所，或餘師所，聞諸世間皆是常等，如是方便入初靜慮乃至有頂，能得清淨、解脫、出離，彼依此見，勇猛精勤；由是因緣，入初靜慮或所餘定。如是入已，能自憶念過去多劫，遂生是見：我及世間皆是常等。從定起已，即於此見堅執不捨；
items.en: What is the one with views in the superior dhyāna? Someone who, from his own teacher or another, has heard that the world and the rest are all permanent, and [believes] that by such means, entering the first dhyāna up to the peak of existence, one can attain purity, liberation, and release. Relying on this view he is valiantly diligent, and by this enters the first dhyāna or another concentration. Having entered thus, he can recollect his own past across many eons, and so gives rise to the view: "self and world are all permanent." Having emerged from the concentration, he clings to this view and will not let it go.

items.zh: 復於後時審思、審慮、審諦觀察。謂由此故，當得清淨、解脫、出離。
items.en: Later, he reflects carefully, considers carefully, and examines carefully, thinking: 'By this I shall attain purity, liberation, and release.'

items.title: Two More Flawed Attainers: Conceit and Doubt

items.zh: 云何慢上靜慮者？謂如有一，聞如是名諸長老等入初靜慮乃至有頂。聞是事已，遂生憍慢：彼既能入靜慮等定，我復何緣而不當入。依止此慢，勇猛精勤；由是因緣，入初靜慮及所餘定。如是入已，後生憍慢。或入定已，作是思惟；唯我能得如是靜慮，餘不能得。彼依此慢，復於後時，於諸靜慮審思、審慮、審諦觀察。
items.en: What is the one with conceit in the superior dhyāna? Someone who hears that such-and-such elders and others have entered the first dhyāna up to the peak of existence, and, hearing this, gives rise to conceit: "if they can enter the dhyānas, why should I not?" Relying on this conceit he is valiantly diligent, and thereby enters the first dhyāna or another concentration. Having entered, he afterwards gives rise to conceit; or, having entered, he thinks: "Only I can attain such dhyāna; others cannot." Relying on this conceit, he later, in the dhyānas, closely thinks, considers, and scrutinises.

items.zh: 云何疑上靜慮者？謂如有一，為性暗鈍，本嘗樂習奢摩他行；由此因緣，入諸靜慮或所餘定。如是入已、復於上定勤修方便，為得未得，於四聖諦勤修現觀；性暗鈍故，不能速證聖諦現觀。由此因緣，於餘所證便生疑惑；依此疑惑，復於勝進審思、審慮、審諦觀察。
items.en: What is the one with doubt in the superior dhyāna? Someone dull by nature who has long delighted in cultivating calm, and thereby enters the dhyānas or another concentration. Having entered, he diligently cultivates the means towards the higher concentrations and towards what is not yet attained; he diligently cultivates the direct realisation of the four noble truths, but being dull by nature cannot quickly realise it. By this, doubt arises in him regarding what else he has realised; relying on this doubt, he again, in advancing, closely thinks, considers, and scrutinises.

items.title: Three Kinds of Concentration (Part 1): Relish-Associated, and Pure

items.zh: 復次，云何愛味相應靜慮等定？謂有鈍根，或貪行故，或煩惱多故。彼唯得聞初靜慮等所有功德，廣說如前愛上靜慮。於上出離不了知故，便生愛味，戀著堅住。其所愛味，當言已出；其能愛味，當言正入。
items.en: Furthermore, what is dhyāna-and-concentration associated with relish? [The practice of] one with dull faculties, or of a greedy disposition, or with many afflictions, who has heard only the merits of the first dhyāna and the rest, as explained above for the relisher of dhyāna. Not understanding release to the higher states, he gives rise to relish, clinging and firmly settling. What is relished should be called "already left"; the relishing should be called "just entered."

items.zh: 云何清淨靜慮等定？謂有中根，或利根性，等煩惱行，或薄塵行。彼從他聞初靜慮等愛味過患及上出離，勇猛精進，入初靜慮或所餘定。如是入已，便能思惟諸定過患，於上出離亦能了知，不生愛味。
items.en: What is pure dhyāna-and-concentration? [The practice of] one with middling or sharp faculties, of an even-affliction or a thin-defilement disposition, who has heard from another of the relish, the faults, and the higher release regarding the first dhyāna and the rest; valiantly diligent, he enters the first dhyāna or another concentration. Having entered, he can contemplate the faults of the concentrations and knows the release to the higher states, and gives rise to no relish.

blocks.text: Fascicle 12 continues the Stage of Meditative Absorption with practical detail: what makes concentration possible, how meditators who have attained the dhyānas still go wrong, and the difference between relished, pure, and uncontaminated concentration. Today: the conditions for absorption and four ways of mishandling it.

Cultivating attention on the thirty-two marks accomplishes four things, among them refining "this attention and its companions". Master Cháng Bǎi: attention is a mental factor; its companion is the mind itself; refining both makes the next moment brighter. Venerable Miào Jìng maps the last item onto the familiar stages of cutting: wearying of the object is the preparatory path, casting off affliction the uninterrupted path, holding firm to severance the path of liberation.

One enters the dhyānas "by four conditions": the power of **cause** (past practice), of **method**, of **teaching**, and of **instruction**. Master Cháng Bǎi's example of the power of cause: the pilgrim Zhìyán, studying meditation in India, mastered in three years what took others ten. The power of teaching includes "dwelling alone in a quiet place". Venerable Miào Jìng: "alone" can mean many people living together without disturbing one another, "as if one person". Solitude is a quality of the community, not only of the place.
Four kinds of people attain the dhyānas and mishandle them:

items: **One who relishes** the dhyāna (愛上靜慮者). Master Cháng Bǎi: 上 praises the dhyāna as a superior attainment; the fault is craving it.
**One with a view**: recalling many past eons, he concludes self and world are permanent (Day 44). Master Cháng Bǎi: "he thinks: from past lives to now, I have always existed."
**One with conceit**: "if they can, why can't I?" Venerable Miào Jìng is generous: "this conceit made him succeed; conceit is an affliction, but affliction can have merit."
**One with doubt**, who doubts even his own attainment. Master Cháng Bǎi: a dull person can still enter absorption if free of karmic obstruction.

blocks.text: Each is a real attainment spoiled by one of the four afflictions of the seventh consciousness: craving, view, conceit, and (here) doubt. Meditation alone does not remove them.

Three kinds of concentration: **relish-associated**, **pure**, and **uncontaminated**. On relish, an exact observation: "What is relished should be called already left; the relishing, just entered." Venerable Miào Jìng: relish is not inside the dhyāna; "only after coming out of it is there relish." We enjoy the memory, not the state.

**Pure concentration** belongs to two types. Venerable Miào Jìng: the "even-affliction" type rarely has active afflictions but does not know their faults; the "thin-defilement" type knows the faults. The second is closer to the path, because knowing the fault is the beginning of insight.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, by what four conditions does one enter the dhyānas up to the peak?
options: the power of cause, of method, of teaching, of instruction
quiz.why: "By four conditions one enters the first dhyāna and so on up to the peak of existence: the power of the cause, the power of method, the power of teaching, and the power of instruction." Venerable Miào Jìng: "having drawn near" may mean threshold concentration or seeds from past lives.

quiz.q: Which monk does Master Cháng Bǎi cite as an example of the "power of the cause"?
options: Zhiyan — travelling to India, he learned in three years what took others ten
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Zhiyan, who went to India for scriptures, studied meditation with an Indian monk and mastered ten years' worth in three" — having neared absorption in past lives. Venerable Miào Jìng: the cause-power is from the past; method-power is present effort, still hopeful.

quiz.q: The power of teaching involves "dwelling alone in a quiet place." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "alone"?
options: many living together without disturbing one another, as if alone — that is "alone"
living in a cave by oneself
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Many living together as if one person — meaning no one disturbs anyone; that's 'alone.'" Master Cháng Bǎi: solitary retreat is recommended only for stream-enterers and above, lest one grow lax. The translation's "dwelling alone" is literal.

quiz.q: The view-bearing attainer recollects many past eons and concludes self and world are permanent. How, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: he reasons that "I" have existed from past lives until now, mind-moments continuing — so life has always gone on
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "He thinks: from past lives to now, I have always existed! Mind-moments continue; my life has gone on from the past till now!" Never separate meditation from the scriptures, or one may mistake the first dhyāna for stream-entry. Venerable Miào Jìng: this is a form-realm attainer's clinging, not scattered thinking.

quiz.q: The conceited attainer thinks "if they can, why can't I?" What does Venerable Miào Jìng say about this conceit?
options: the conceit drove him to success, which isn't bad; conceit is affliction, yet affliction too has merit — this is "reckoning oneself equal"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "This conceit made him succeed — not bad; conceit is an affliction, but affliction can have merit"; "'he can enter, so can I' — I'm the same as you — that's 'reckoning equal.'" Thinking "only I can" afterwards is reckoning superior.

quiz.q: "What is relished should be called already left; the relishing, just entered." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain this?
options: relish isn't inside the dhyāna — it comes after emerging from it
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "When he relishes, he isn't inside the dhyāna; only after coming out of it is there relish." Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Abhidharmakośa*: there are three kinds — relish-associated, pure, and uncontaminated.

quiz.q: Pure concentration belongs to the "even-affliction" or "thin-defilement" type. How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish them?
options: the even-affliction type rarely gives rise to affliction but doesn't know its faults; the thin-defilement type does know them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "This person rarely has afflictions — greed, hatred, delusion, conceit barely stir — but doesn't know that affliction has faults"; the thin-defilement type does. Master Cháng Bǎi: the even type has every affliction, none severe.
